CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right index finger injury

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
42-year-old female presents with right index finger injury sustained during a skiing accident that occurred last Saturday. Patient reports she was skiing on double black diamonds when she lost control and fell, jamming her right index finger during the fall. The injury occurred approximately 5 days prior to presentation. Patient rates her pain at 7 out of 10. She has tried ibuprofen for pain relief without significant improvement. Patient denies applying ice or a splint to the finger prior to this visit. She reports this was her only injury sustained from the fall.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Chronic constipation
Appendectomy at age 7

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for chronic constipation

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient engages in skiing.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Examination of the right index finger reveals pain on palpation, pain with traction, and pain with compression over the distal interphalangeal joint and an adjacent joint. X-ray of the right hand is reviewed and shows normal alignment of all joints and bones with no fractures.

RESULTS
Right hand x-ray: Normal, no fractures, normal bone and joint alignment.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Sprain of the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint of the right index finger. Treatment plan: (1) Apply splint to right index finger; (2) Prescribe Mobic 15 mg orally once daily for 14 doses; (3) Follow-up visit in 2 weeks to assess healing; (4) Consider hand physical therapy at follow-up visit if indicated.
